one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent designed decompress.py to restore files into a sibling '_restored' directory instead of in-place, and compress.py created 130+ shard subdirectories in the output root (far exceeding the 30-item-per-directory limit), violating both core task requirements.
t_err_evidence: compress.py written to relative app/ directory instead of required absolute /app path
t_commit_evidence: By step 8, both core scripts are written and locked in with their fundamental design flaws: compress.py will produce hundreds of shard directories in the output root, and decompress.py will always restore to a '_restored' sibling rather than in-place. All subsequent work builds on and refines these scripts without changing their core architecture.
t_surface_evidence: Error during decompression: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'test_output_restored/c4-mini-00000-of-10000.jsonl'
trigger_explanation: The agent never carefully read or internalized two core task requirements: (1) that decompression must restore files in-place within the provided resharded directory, and (2) that every directory in the output must have at most 30 items (meaning nested directory hierarchies are required). Instead, it designed a flat shard scheme with hundreds of subdirectories and an out-of-place restore target, proceeding confidently without verifying compliance with either constraint.
